about.heading: Independent Ansible® Learning Tool
about.intro: Ansible101 is an independent, browser-based site for tutorials, reviews, visual explanations, debugging walkthroughs, and safe experimentation with Ansible playbooks and Jinja expressions. The project is intended to help learners and practitioners understand automation logic more quickly by turning YAML into visual flows and plain-English explanations.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.body: Tutorials, reviews, playbook breakdowns, and hands-on exploration of Ansible logic without needing a remote host or a running control node.

independence.title: Independence
independence.body: This site is community-built and is not an official documentation portal, support channel, training product, or certification service.

trademark.title: Trademark Notice
trademark.body: Ansible101 is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Red Hat, Inc. Ansible® is a trademark of Red Hat, LLC, registered in the United States and other countries.

legalSummary.title: Legal Summary
legalSummary.para1: Ansible101 exists to provide independent commentary, education, review, and experimentation tooling around Ansible concepts. References to Ansible modules, playbooks, terminology, or trademarks are used solely to describe compatibility, explain workflows, and support learning.
legalSummary.para2: Nothing on this site should be interpreted as official Red Hat guidance, product support, certification material, or vendor-authorized training. Users should refer to official vendor documentation for authoritative product behavior, licensing, support terms, and trademark policy.

modeTabs.title: Mode Switcher
modeTabs.description: Switch between Playbook, Snippet, Jinja2, and Limits views. Each mode is independent - your content is preserved when you switch.

editorPane.title: YAML Editor
editorPane.description: Paste or type your Ansible playbook here. The editor gives you syntax highlighting, error squiggles, and line-level highlighting when you click a flow node.

fileExplorer.title: File Explorer
fileExplorer.description: Add extra task files (include_tasks, role files, scripts) as tabs here. Drag tabs to reorder. The flow resolves cross-file task references automatically.

flowPane.title: Execution Flow
flowPane.description: A live graph of every play, task and handler in the playbook. Click any node to jump to it in the editor and see a plain-English explanation on the right.

humanSidebar.title: Human Explanation
humanSidebar.description: Explains the selected task or play in plain English - what module is used, what it does, and any conditions or loops applied.

btnVars.title: Playbook Vars
btnVars.description: Override vars and vars_files values defined in the playbook. Useful for testing different variable combinations without editing the YAML.

btnFacts.title: Mock Ansible Facts
btnFacts.description: Simulate ansible_facts - the host variables Ansible collects at runtime. The flow and Jinja2 renderer use these to evaluate when conditions and variable expressions.

viewTabs.title: Variable Resolver
viewTabs.description: This tab answers a classic Ansible question: "I set this variable in 3 places - which one actually wins?" Switching you there now.

resolverPickers.title: Pick What You're Resolving
resolverPickers.description: Two dropdowns: which inventory and which host. Variables can resolve differently for every host - change either and the table updates instantly. (To resolve a different playbook, switch the active playbook in the toolbar above.)

resolverActions.title: Send Vars Elsewhere
resolverActions.description: Found a value worth testing somewhere else? Use in Flow loads this host's resolved variables into the Execution Flow tab. Jinja2 loads them into the Jinja2 sandbox.

resolverGroups.title: Group Membership
resolverGroups.description: Every inventory group this host belongs to, and every play that targets it. This matters because group_vars only apply to hosts actually in that group.

resolverFilters.title: Narrow the List
resolverFilters.description: Filter searches by name. Referenced only hides variables your playbook never actually uses. Show facts reveals Ansible's built-in ansible_* facts (hidden by default - there are a lot of them).

resolverExtravars.title: Extra Vars (-e)
resolverExtravars.description:
Simulates running ansible-playbook -e .... Pick a vars file, or type key=value pairs.

These always win over every other source - that's precedence level L22, the highest there is.

resolverMocks.title: Mock Runtime Values
resolverMocks.description: Some variables only exist while a playbook is actually running - facts, register results, role params. Give them a test value here so the table (and Jinja2 expressions) resolve instead of showing "undefined".

resolverTable.title: The "L" Badges = Priority Ranking
resolverTable.description:
Every variable gets a badge like L11 or L12. Think of it as a priority ranking from 1 to 22 - L1 is the weakest source, L22 is the strongest.

Bigger number always wins - no matter where it appears in your files. That's why L12 (play vars:) beats L11 (host facts) here, even though facts are usually "more specific."

Hover any badge to see its full name. Click a row to see every place that variable was set, ranked.

resolverStack.title: See Every Place It Was Set
resolverStack.description:
Clicking a row opens this panel - it lists every place that variable was defined, not just the winner, ranked by precedence. (Selected one for you below.)

The green entry on top won. Greyed-out entries below were shadowed - they were set, but a higher level overrode them. The small ↗ icon links to Ansible's official precedence docs.

btnShare.title: Share
btnShare.description: Copies a URL to your clipboard that encodes the current playbook and extra files. Anyone with the link opens exactly what you see.

modeTabs.title: Snippet Mode
modeTabs.description: Paste a single Ansible task here to get an instant visual breakdown - no full playbook needed.

editorPane.title: Task YAML
editorPane.description:
Paste one task in YAML format. For example: 
- name: Install nginx
  apt:
    name: nginx
    state: present
The card updates as you type.

snippetPane.title: Quick Card
snippetPane.description: A visual breakdown of the task: the module used, each parameter, any when conditions, loops, and tags - all explained in plain English.

btnFacts.title: Mock Facts
btnFacts.description: Provide mock facts to evaluate when conditions and Jinja2 expressions inside the task.

modeTabs.title: Jinja2 Mode
modeTabs.description: A sandbox for Ansible's Jinja2 templating engine. Paste any expression to trace how it evaluates step by step.

editorPane.title: Jinja2 Expression
editorPane.description: Enter any Jinja2 template - variable lookups, filters, conditionals, loops. Example: {{ inventory_hostname | upper }}

jinja2Pane.title: Pipeline View
jinja2Pane.description: Shows each step in the evaluation pipeline: variable substitution → filters applied → final output. Hover a step to see the intermediate value.

btnFacts.title: Mock Facts
btnFacts.description: Define the variables the Jinja2 expression can reference. Add your own hostnames, IPs, custom variables - anything the template expects.

modeTabs.title: Limits Mode
modeTabs.description: A sandbox for testing Ansible's --limit flag. Build an inventory, write a pattern, and instantly see which hosts match.

inventoryEditor.title: Inventory Editor
inventoryEditor.description: Define your inventory visually - add groups, add hosts to groups, or import a real inventory file (JSON from ansible-inventory --list, INI, or YAML).

inventoryImport.title: Import Inventory
inventoryImport.description: Click Import or paste / drag-and-drop an inventory file directly onto this panel. Supports ansible-inventory --list JSON, classic INI, and YAML formats.

limitInput.title: Limit Pattern
limitInput.description: Type an Ansible --limit pattern. Examples: web:db (union), web:&production (intersection), all:!staging (exclusion), web-0* (wildcard). Autocomplete suggests groups and hosts as you type.

limitResults.title: Match Results
limitResults.description: Every group is shown with its hosts. Matched hosts are highlighted in green, excluded hosts are dimmed. Click any host to open its detail panel.
